source: Issue #944; AGENTS.md 'After dispatch...' paragraph (the real #869 conflict hunk)
baseText: After dispatch, first evaluate the READY immediate-dispatch gate, before the Decomposition boundary below and before any other tool call: when the dispatched issue could plausibly be a control-plane issue (its number was given directly, or a parent snapshot points at it as the current control issue), the session's first action is `node tools/orchestration/session-entry-gate.mjs --control-issue <N>` (issue #675/#676: this wrapper composes `ready-dispatch-gate.mjs` with every mechanically authorized `actionEnvelope.mode: "chain"` follow-up gate internally, per `docs/operating-model.md` § Session-entry gate, and its own process exit reports only a genuine operational failure — never an internal leaf gate's own domain exit code for an expected lifecycle branch such as `REVIEW`; its JSON output carries the final resolved verdict's own fields verbatim, plus a `provenance` trail, so every verdict-handling instruction below still applies unchanged, whether the JSON came from this wrapper or a leaf gate invoked directly) — never a freeform `gh issue view` on that same issue first, and never with a hand-typed `--repo <owner>/<repo>`: the gate derives current repository identity deterministically from the checkout's own configured remote (issue #344), so the normal path never asks the controller to remember, infer, or type it; issue #321 is the record of two independent live sessions that read the control issue by hand and, in that same investigative step, also read the linked thick execution issue and queried unrelated PRs before dispatching, exactly the failure this script exists to make structurally impossible. Every pre-PR terminal verdict this gate returns (`READY_TO_DISPATCH`, `READY_TO_DISPATCH_PLANNING`, `READY_TO_RUN_DISPATCH_MANIFEST`, `READY_TO_DISPATCH_UNITS`, `READY_TO_DISPATCH_INTEGRATION`, `READY_TO_PROJECT_PLAN_READY`, `READY_TO_PROJECT_ROUTED`, `REPLAN_REQUIRED`) carries a literal `stopAfter: true` field (issue #498 unit 498-A, mirroring `next-review-transition-gate.mjs`'s own established convention) — a mandatory, literal stop, reached only once that verdict's own required durable output (and, for the two `READY_TO_PROJECT_*` verdicts, the thin-control projection itself) is verified, never license to keep reasoning into the next transition in the same invocation. On `READY_TO_DISPATCH`, dispatch the linked execution worker immediately by reference (issue number, controlling issue, route, all taken from the script's own output) and stop, with no other tool call in between — without reading that execution issue's body, judging its decomposition shape, or doing implementation reconnaissance first. Build the dispatch prompt by piping the gate's JSON output into `node tools/orchestration/format-dispatch-prompt.mjs` and using its stdout verbatim as the worker's prompt — do not compose the prompt by hand. On `READY_TO_DISPATCH_PLANNING`, pipe the same gate JSON into `format-dispatch-prompt.mjs` and dispatch the planning worker by reference, then stop. On `READY_TO_RUN_DISPATCH_MANIFEST`, run `node tools/orchestration/prepare-dispatch-manifest.mjs --execution-issue <N> --create` (or `--comment-id <id>` when updating an existing manifest) so the manifest is persisted durably, then compose the control Issue's own body with `Lifecycle: ROUTED` and persist it via `node tools/orchestration/write-control-snapshot.mjs --control-issue <N> --body-file -` before stopping — a durably persisted, verified manifest alone is not the breakpoint; the projected thin-control state is (issue #498 unit 498-A, closing #498 Live reproduction C, where a verified manifest existed but Lifecycle stayed `PLAN_READY` and a fresh controller re-ran Route/Prepare). On `READY_TO_PROJECT_PLAN_READY` / `READY_TO_PROJECT_ROUTED` (issue #498 unit 498-A, the 2026-09-10 #500 stranded-state fix: the gate found `READY_FOR_PLAN`/`PLAN_READY` but durable state shows a valid plan/verified manifest already exists — a prior planning or Route/Prepare session converged the durable artifact and correctly stopped per its own fresh-session boundary, but the *projection* into thin control state never happened, so `Lifecycle` stayed stale), persist the gate's own returned `proposedBody` verbatim via `node tools/orchestration/write-control-snapshot.mjs --control-issue <N> --body-file -` and stop — do not dispatch a redundant planning worker or re-run Route/Prepare merely because Lifecycle was stale; the gate's own idempotent recognition (`ready-dispatch-gate.mjs`'s `probeExistingPlan`/`verifyRoutedDispatchManifest`) already confirmed the durable artifact is valid, so no further verification is required before this write. On `READY_TO_DISPATCH_UNITS`, dispatch only the currently `dispatch_ready=true` units from a Dispatch Manifest that the gate has just verified from durable authority (non-`none` Plan Index pointer, comment identity on the same execution Issue, required manifest heading, and matching Plan Index backlink) — compose each unit's own dispatch prompt with `node tools/orchestration/format-unit-dispatch-prompt.mjs --execution-issue <N> --unit <UnitID>` (issue #498 unit 498-A: the formatter this verdict previously had no explicitly named consumer for — do not hand-compose a unit dispatch prompt) — and stop once that wave is durable. On `READY_TO_DISPATCH_INTEGRATION`, pipe the gate JSON into `format-dispatch-prompt.mjs`, dispatch the integration/PR worker by reference, and stop once the PR/Stage 1 durable breakpoint is recorded. On `REPLAN_REQUIRED` — issue #498 unit 498-B, closing the #407/#408 and #454/#455 (via #434) reproductions: while evaluating `Lifecycle: PLAN_READY`, `ready-dispatch-gate.mjs` found that `prepare-dispatch-manifest.mjs`'s own routing computation (run as a dry probe, nothing persisted) would resolve one or more plan units to `route=REPLAN_REQUIRED` — pipe the gate JSON into `format-dispatch-prompt.mjs` (it selects the "Planning-correction worker dispatch" template from the verdict's own `state` field) and dispatch a planning-correction worker by reference (execution/control Issue numbers, the Plan Index URL, and the failing unit IDs — all taken from the gate's own output) and stop. Do not read the thick execution Issue, Worker Unit Contract bodies, the Shared Contract body, or routing/parser source to diagnose the failure yourself first — the gate's own compact `planIndexUrl`/`replanRequiredUnitIds`/`reason` fields, and the dispatched worker's own direct read of the plan/unit authority it is pointed at, are sufficient; report the verdict's own `reason` in chat if a concise handoff is needed, but never restate it into the dispatch prompt. That worker uses #497's deterministic writer/validator to persist a corrected plan and returns only a compact confirmation; a later fresh invocation of this same gate against the still-`PLAN_READY` control Issue then re-evaluates exactly as it would for a plan that never hit `REPLAN_REQUIRED`, converging on the identical `READY_TO_RUN_DISPATCH_MANIFEST`/`READY_TO_PROJECT_ROUTED` boundary above — no special-cased "recovered" verdict exists or is needed. A genuinely ambiguous routing failure still fails closed to this same verdict; never invent a default/fuzzy route on the controller's behalf. A live #321 proof (`docs/diagnostic-traces/615f2b4a-69eb-42f1-bef6-432a4e32f4dc.json`) recorded a controller that correctly skipped every pre-dispatch read and still hand-composed a 2554-character prompt by restating AGENTS.md's own general contract sections into it — a distinct reference-only-size violation from the #283/#314 read-before-dispatch defect, closed the same way: by removing the composition step's freedom to grow, not by adding another prose reminder to compose carefully. That linked issue's own decomposition shape is the dispatched worker's concern, not a prerequisite the controller must resolve before handing off; see Subagent dispatch below for the two-plane read this gate protects, and `docs/operating-model.md` § Two-plane Issue dispatch for the closed exceptions (malformed/conflicting control state, an unresolved escalation, or similar) that still permit direct inspection. On `AUDIT_ISSUE_DETECTED` — issue #407 unit 407-B, the #432 fix: the dispatched Issue is itself a directly-dispatched canonical Stage 2 Audit Issue, not a thin control Issue — run `node tools/orchestration/next-review-transition-gate.mjs --audit-issue <N>` (the `<N>` the gate's own output names) and act on *its* verdict: `STAGE2_CLOSE_READY` invokes the verdict's own `nextCommand` verbatim (real run) and stops — `lifecycle-gate.mjs close-audit` alone when there is no gated work issue, chained after `lifecycle-gate.mjs close-work-issue` first when one exists, per the PR #435 Stage 1 review finding that `close-audit` deliberately never touches the work issue on its own; `STAGE2_REPORT_READY_TO_RECORD` (issue #439: a completed Stage 2 report already exists on the thread but the durable `Verdict` field is still `PENDING`/malformed — the live #408/#436 gap, where a controller described a genuinely completed CLEAN report as "no completed response has landed" solely because the dropdown had not been promoted) runs the verdict's own `nextCommand` (the real, non-dry-run `lifecycle-gate.mjs record-verdict` invocation) verbatim and stops — this promotes the already-established evidence into the durable field without re-adjudicating it; a fresh invocation afterward resolves the now-recorded verdict through this same gate; `STAGE2_CORRECTION_REQUIRED` pipes the gate JSON into `format-dispatch-prompt.mjs` (issue #570: it recognizes this state directly and renders a fixed "Stage 2 correction worker dispatch" template, extended by issue #646 to mandate opening/linking one correction PR, requesting Stage 1 at its head, and running `finalize-pr-breakpoint.mjs` before that worker reports — closing the #487/#643/#644/#645 live reproduction where a correction worker's own "push it, and stop" contract left the thin control durably pointed at the pre-correction PR/audit state, so a fresh dispatch produced a duplicate correction PR) to dispatch one correction worker by reference and stops; `STAGE2_CORRECTION_PR_NEEDS_FINALIZATION` (issue #646, the same live reproduction's duplicate-dispatch half: the gate's own reconciliation — `reconcileStage2CorrectionPr`, the Stage 2 analog of `ready-dispatch-gate.mjs`'s existing `reconcileReadyPrBreakpoint`, issue #456 unit 456-B — found an already-open, work-Issue-linked correction PR while evaluating what would otherwise be `STAGE2_CORRECTION_REQUIRED`, meaning a prior correction worker already crossed the PR boundary but the durable control projection never landed) runs the verdict's own `nextCommand` verbatim (the same idempotent Stage 1 trigger, then `finalize-pr-breakpoint.mjs`, that verdict's own worker route performs) and stops — never dispatch a second correction worker against this same finding merely because Lifecycle is still `AUDIT`; `finalize-pr-breakpoint.mjs` itself now accepts `Lifecycle: AUDIT` as a recognized pre-finalize source state for exactly this route; `STAGE2_RESPONSE_UNUSABLE` (issue #447, live reproductions #446 and #380's first round: a genuine, provenance-valid, *substantive* bot response — one showing at least a commit reference, an explicit verdict, or verification-results content, per a Stage 1 review finding on the #447 PR itself — landed post-trigger, but none of the genuine substantive bot response(s) on the thread is a completed Stage 2 audit report under the current evidence contract; a bare progress/kickoff acknowledgement carrying none of those signals (the issue #229 "Starting #178." shape) is deliberately excluded and resolves as ordinary `NO_ACTION_YET` instead, so a routine Stage 2 kickoff never becomes a founder interrupt — this is a distinct, recognized fail-closed state, never ordinary waiting and never AMBIGUOUS's "this gate does not recognize the state" meaning) stops immediately with the repository's normal concise blocked/founder-interrupt chat contract, quoting only the verdict's own compact `postAudit`/`reportEvidence` reference (the audit Issue and the genuine-but-unusable response's own comment URL) — do not automatically retrigger Stage 2 or coach the reviewer toward a different reply shape (issue #259's anti-coaching authority applies here exactly as it does to any other post-response Stage 2 state), and do not re-run the gate speculatively hoping the state changes: re-running against the same durable evidence deterministically reproduces the same verdict, and it only changes once a later genuine, complete bot response lands on the thread on its own; `STAGE2_TRIGGER_REQUIRED` (issue #735, the live #398/#729/PR #733/Audit #734 reproduction: `lifecycle-gate.mjs post-audit` found a canonical, exact-merge, OPEN, PENDING Audit Issue whose thread carries no valid Stage 2 reviewer trigger at all — prepared but never triggered; before this fix that exact shape resolved to terminal `NO_ACTION_YET`, so independent review was never actually requested even though the control-facing state looked like ordinary waiting) runs the verdict's own `nextCommand` verbatim — the one remaining idempotent `tools/review-watch/trigger.mjs --kind issue` invocation, safe to retry because `trigger.mjs`'s own dedup (`findExistingTrigger`) never posts a second trigger once one exists — and stops; `checkPostAudit` itself re-verifies, immediately before returning this state, that the referenced Audit Issue is still OPEN, carries the complete canonical audit shape (`hasCanonicalAuditShape`), and remains the sole matching candidate for its own recorded exact-merge/work identity (`findMatchingOpenAuditIssues`) — issue #736 Stage 1 correction, closing the gap where a stale, closed, superseded, or malformed Audit Issue could otherwise reach this verdict and consume the one permitted reviewer trigger on unverified state — so this routing performs no additional inspection of its own; a revalidation failure never reaches `STAGE2_TRIGGER_REQUIRED` at all, it falls through to the same `AMBIGUOUS` fail-closed stop this paragraph already names next, never an improvised recovery; `NO_ACTION_YET`/`AMBIGUOUS` stop per their existing meaning elsewhere in this file. Do not read the linked execution/work Issue, inspect `stage2-report.mjs`'s source, or write an ad hoc parser script to resolve this by hand — the #432 live reproduction is exactly that avoidable detour. On `BLOCKED` — issue #368: the control Issue was read successfully and its own recorded fields explicitly say the current invocation must not advance (a blocking lifecycle value — the ad hoc bullet convention's `Lifecycle: BLOCKED`, or the shipped template's `State: BLOCKED_FAILURE`/`State: BLOCKED_EXTERNAL`, issue #370 — a non-`none` Blocker, or an unresolved Founder decision) — stop immediately with the repository's normal concise blocked/founder-interrupt chat contract, using only the gate's own compact `reasons` output — except that when those `reasons` name a non-`none` Blocker, the controller's one permitted step before treating this as a genuine stop is exactly one invocation of `node tools/orchestration/reconcile-control-blocker.mjs --control-issue <N>` (issue #437; see `docs/operating-model.md` § Live interrupt state and blocker reconciliation): an `UNBLOCKED` result means re-invoke `ready-dispatch-gate.mjs` fresh and proceed from that verdict, and any other result (`INCOMPLETE_PREREQUISITE`, `AMBIGUOUS_BLOCKER`, `ALREADY_UNBLOCKED`, `ALREADY_TERMINAL`) stops with this same concise chat contract, unchanged. Do not first read the linked thick execution Issue, inspect its requirements or acceptance criteria, search related Issues/PRs, inspect repository implementation surfaces, try to solve or work around the blocker, reinterpret the blocker as authorization for a different experiment or implementation path, or mutate the blocked control/execution state merely to create work for itself. Control #301's live reproduction is the incident this closes: a fresh `work on #301` read a control Issue with `Lifecycle: BLOCKED` and an active Blocker, and — because the old gate returned the same broad `NOT_READY` verdict for that case as for an ordinary non-control-shaped issue — the controller then began its own investigation and repository work around linked execution Issue #297 instead of stopping. `BLOCKED` is a distinct gate verdict from `NOT_READY` by construction specifically so that collapse cannot recur; do not treat it as a variant of `NOT_READY`'s fallthrough. On `NOT_READY` — the immediate-dispatch shortcut genuinely does not apply and no field explicitly asserts a stop: a mid-cycle non-`BLOCKED` lifecycle state (EXECUTING, VERIFYING, REVIEW, AUDIT, CORRECTION), or the issue is plainly not control-plane-shaped, e.g. a legacy unsplit issue with no "Current state" bullet block, which reads as NOT_READY rather than as an error — the gate simply does not apply — fall through to the Decomposition boundary below and reason normally, including reading the issue's own body directly. Two exceptions do not fall through to free reasoning: a post-PR mid-cycle lifecycle state (EXECUTING, VERIFYING, REVIEW, AUDIT, CORRECTION) — `docs/operating-model.md` § Watched lifecycle breakpoints, "Deterministic post-PR transition resolution" governs that case instead, via its own deterministic gate; and a stale `Lifecycle: EXECUTION_COMPLETE` whose own `- **PR:**`/`- **Stage 1:**` bullets already show the PR/review boundary crossed (issue #444: the gate's `NOT_READY` verdict then carries a truthy `postPrLifecycle` field, e.g. `EXECUTION_COMPLETE_PR_ESTABLISHED`) — that case resolves through the identical deterministic post-PR gate as the first exception, even though the durable `Lifecycle` text has not yet been rewritten to one of the five mid-cycle values above. Both exceptions are exactly what the verdict's own `actionEnvelope.mode: "chain"` already encodes (see below); this prose and that machine field must never diverge on which `NOT_READY` shapes chain versus fall through. Stage 1 review finding on this PR (issue #344): when the gate script itself errors instead — missing `--control-issue`, an unreadable control Issue, or a repository-identity resolution failure — that is not a verdict on the control Issue's content at all, and must never be treated as the same permission: a script error means authoritative control state was never reached, so it must not itself authorize decomposition, execution-Issue inspection, or implementation reconnaissance merely because the deterministic check failed. Repair the underlying cause first (e.g. a missing/misconfigured `origin` remote, or a mistyped `--control-issue`) and rerun the gate; if the error persists, treat it as a Founder interrupt condition (a failed safety/correctness gate with no authorized recovery path) rather than reasoning past it.

see `docs/operating-model.md` § Control-plane runner freshness) (issue #675/#676: this wrapper composes `ready-dispatch-gate.mjs` with every mechanically authorized `actionEnvelope.mode: "chain"` follow-up gate internally, per `docs/operating-model.md` § Session-entry gate, and its own process exit reports only a genuine operational failure — never an internal leaf gate's own domain exit code for an expected lifecycle branch such as `REVIEW`;
